title: Electronic Structure and Periodic Properties of Elements

variables.meaning: the wavelength of a wave, the distance between two consecutive peaks or troughs
the frequency of a wave, the number of wave cycles that pass a specified point in space per unit time
the speed of light in a vacuum, 2.998 × 10⁸ m/s, which is the product of the wavelength and the frequency
the energy of one photon, or the quantized vibrational energy of Planck’s treatment
Planck’s constant, 6.626 × 10⁻³⁴ J s
the whole number that counts the half-wavelengths of a standing wave, or the quanta of Planck’s vibrational energies
the wavelength at which a blackbody curve has its maximum
the temperature of a blackbody, the single parameter on which its distribution depends
the Rydberg constant, 1.097 × 10⁷ m⁻¹
the constant of Balmer’s empirical equation for the visible lines of hydrogen
the energy of an electron in the Bohr orbit with quantum number n, measured from the ionization limit and so always negative
the difference between the orbital energies an electron moves between, which is the energy of the photon emitted or absorbed
the quantum number of a Bohr orbit, a positive integer that labels one of the allowed orbits and takes no value between them
the nuclear charge, which is +1 for hydrogen, +2 for He⁺, +3 for Li²⁺ and so on
the constant of Bohr’s equation for the energy of the electron, made of fundamental constants such as the electron mass and charge and Planck's constant, with a value of 2.179 × 10⁻¹⁸ J
the radius of the circular orbit an electron is allowed to move in
the Bohr radius, the radius of the ground-state orbit of hydrogen, with a value of 5.292 × 10⁻¹¹ m
the energy of the orbit the electron starts in
the energy of the orbit the electron ends in
the wavelength of the photon emitted or absorbed when an electron moves between two orbits
the frequency of that photon, to which its energy is proportional
Planck's constant, 6.626 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, which ties a photon's energy to its frequency
the speed of light in a vacuum, 2.998 × 10⁸ m/s
the Rydberg constant, which Bohr's model recovers as the quotient k/hc
the de Broglie wavelength of a particle of mass m moving with velocity v
the mass of the particle
the velocity of the particle, not to be confused with the frequency ν
the linear momentum of the particle, the product of its mass and velocity
the radius of the circular orbit that the electron wave must fit
the uncertainty in the position of a particle
the uncertainty in the momentum of a particle along x
Planck’s constant divided by 2π, 1.055 × 10⁻³⁴ J s
the wavefunction of an electron, whose squared magnitude gives the probability of finding it near a point in space
the total energy of the quantum particle in the Schrödinger equation
the energy change of an electronic transition, positive when a photon is absorbed and negative when one is emitted
the principal quantum number, 1, 2, 3, …, which names the shell
the principal quantum number of the initial energy state
the principal quantum number of the final energy state
the secondary (angular momentum) quantum number, 0 to n − 1, which names the subshell and the shape of the orbital
the magnetic quantum number, −l to +l, which gives the orientation of the orbital
the spin quantum number, +1/2 or −1/2
the nuclear charge, the number of protons in the nucleus
the effective nuclear charge, the pull the nucleus exerts on one electron once the shielding of the others is taken into account
an ionization energy, the energy required to remove an electron from a gaseous atom or ion; IE₁ for the first electron, IE₂ for the second
the electron affinity, the energy change when a gaseous atom accepts an electron
the covalent radius of an atom, one-half the distance between the nuclei of two identical atoms joined by a covalent bond
